source.title: Reasoning Circuits in Language Models: A Mechanistic Interpretation of Syllogistic Inference
source.authors: Geonhee Kim; Marco Valentino; André Freitas

record.tranche_reason: The study uses circuit discovery and intervention rather than representation-similarity measures to test whether interpretable reasoning circuits recur across models (V5).
record.gate_note: The study reports circuit patterns across model sizes and families, which bear on recurrence of interpretable circuits. Task accuracies in Table 3 and Figure 6 are not results measuring circuit recurrence, so they are not separate rows. Detailed activation-patching plots are described qualitatively in the text; no numerical circuit-similarity measure is reported.
record.test_reason: The study checks by activation patching and logit lens whether its GPT-2 medium syllogism circuit (middle-term suppression plus mover heads) recurs in other sizes and families. That bears directly on V5's recurrence of circuits across models. The comparisons are qualitative, read from patching plots, with suppression heads picked by hand.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors conclude that the circuit generalizes across schemes, sizes and architectures in sufficiently scaled models. Small models show erratic patterns, and Qwen shows a distinct but comparable suppression. They add that the mechanism is contaminated by world knowledge, with more complex head contributions at larger sizes.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses activation patching, circuit ablation, and logit-lens analysis of syllogistic reasoning circuits; it does not use the representation-similarity measurements in the original sources.
record.method_sensitivity: Model size and family change the reported pattern: smaller Pythia models are erratic, GPT-2 small reverses in the all-term residual-stream setup, and Qwen suppresses at the last token rather than [p].

fits_no_version.finding: Compatible circuit patterns appear only in models above roughly 0.4B parameters. Smaller models are erratic, and head contributions grow more complex with size.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Recurrence of a task circuit across models grows with model scale and task competence (a circuit-level analogue of V1).

fits_no_version.finding: The fine-tuned GPT-2 medium yields activation patterns nearly indistinguishable from the pre-trained model.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Circuits formed in pre-training persist through fine-tuning.

record.peer_reviewed: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
record.problems: The cross-model circuit comparisons are primarily qualitative and rely on activation-pattern analyses; the study does not report a numerical measure of circuit similarity. The authors also note that the analysis is limited to specific syllogistic templates and focuses predominantly on transitivity and term-specific information.
record.rows_left_out: Table 3 and Figure 6 task-accuracy results were not extracted as rows because accuracy does not measure recurrence of interpretable circuits. Detailed plot-only head and activation results were not separately enumerated where the text gives only grouped qualitative conclusions.

untested.parts: No representational-alignment measure between independently trained models as a function of scale.
No vision-language or paired cross-modal data.
No mapping, stitching or relative representations between models.

Only one task-specific circuit (syllogistic completion, symbolic inputs) is compared. Individual neurons, SAE features and other circuits are not tested, and there is no quantitative circuit-similarity score.
No comparison of similarity metrics or of input distributions for convergence.
No test of plateau or of shared-data explanations for alignment.

missing.what: The statement that Pythia-70M/160M 'mirror the limitations seen in under-scaled models like GPT-2 small'. This qualifies R2's 'similar patterns' reading and is not reflected in R2's value.

Per-model accuracies in Table 3 (e.g. Pythia-160M symbolic 0.00; Pythia-410M 0.99; Qwen 1.00). They are needed to read the groupings as competence-dependent. The record declares them left out, but researchers comparing studies would need them as context.

record.verdict_notes: All cross-model evidence is qualitative inspection of patching and logit-lens plots (Figures 10–12), with m-suppression heads selected manually per model. No numerical circuit-similarity measure is given. Necessity and sufficiency ablations were run only on GPT-2 medium, not on the other models. Appendix J frames the work under the universality hypothesis, citing Li et al. 2015.

versions.untested_parts: The study does not measure whether representations of independently trained models with different architectures, objectives, or data become more aligned as size and capability increase.
No paired image-caption or other vision-language representations are examined.
The study does not compare models trained from different initializations of the same architecture.
No representation mapping, stitching, relative-representation, or unpaired alignment method is tested.
The study tests recurrence of syllogistic reasoning circuits, not recurrence of individual neurons or SAE features, nor universal features across tasks beyond the tested syllogisms.
The study does not compare representation-similarity metrics, their settings, or in-distribution versus out-of-distribution inputs.
The study does not test whether representation alignment plateaus or whether shared training data or objectives explain such alignment.

rows.subject: GPT-2 Medium
rows.operation_detail: Activation patching and circuit analysis identified a symbolic syllogistic reasoning circuit.
rows.measure: Identified circuit pattern: middle-term suppression and information propagation via mover heads
rows.value: The study identifies a circuit with a middle-term suppression head and mover heads; the circuit is described as necessary and sufficient for symbolic arguments.
rows.note: This is the reference circuit used in the study's cross-model comparisons.
rows.check: This is the circuit discovery in the reference model itself. A single model cannot show recurrence across models, so the row is the reference, not evidence for V5.

rows.subject: GPT-2 small
rows.operation_detail: Applied symbolic-circuit intervention analysis across model sizes.
rows.measure: Suppression mechanism patterns and information flow compared with the identified circuit
rows.value: The text reports similar suppression mechanism patterns and information flow across GPT-2 sizes.
rows.note: The reported similarity is qualified by a reversed residual-stream result in the all-term corruption setup, recorded separately in R3.
rows.check: Section 4.3 reports similar suppression patterns, but the all-term residual stream is reversed (R3). Section 4.4 also groups GPT-2 small with 'under-scaled models' showing erratic patterns, so recurrence is incomplete, not full.

rows.subject: GPT-2 small
rows.value: The residual-stream result is described as reversed; the text attributes this to low downstream accuracy.
rows.note: This is an exception to the broader similarity reported across GPT-2 sizes.
rows.check: A reversed residual-stream pattern means this part of the circuit does not recur. That is not an effect opposite to V5, so 'absent' fits better than 'reversed'.

rows.subject: GPT-2 medium (Fine-tuned for Critical Thinking)
rows.operation_detail: Applied symbolic-circuit intervention analysis to a fine-tuned model and compared its activation patterns with the pre-trained counterpart.
rows.measure: Similarity of activation patterns to the pre-trained GPT-2 medium circuit
rows.value: Activation patterns are described as nearly indistinguishable from the pre-trained counterpart.
rows.note: The authors infer that the core circuit originates from pre-training rather than fine-tuning.
rows.check: The fine-tuned GPT-2 medium is derived from the same pre-trained weights. Its match to the original shows the circuit survives fine-tuning, not that it recurs in an independently trained model.

relationships.condition: GPT-2 large and XL; Pythia-410M and 1B; Llama-3.2-1B (symbolic syllogisms)
relationships.reason: These models show information flow and middle-term suppression compatible with the GPT-2 medium circuit (R4, R5, R8, R9, R10). GPT-2 large and XL show more complex head contributions.
relationships.display_finding: Information flow and middle-term suppression resembled the GPT-2 medium circuit, with more complex head contributions in GPT-2 large and XL.
